candidates.title: Gryffin, Łaszewo, AR/CO
candidates.summary: Gryffin headlines the outdoor park under the Kosciuszko Bridge on Saturday Oct 17 with Łaszewo and AR/CO, part of the Bowery Presents 2026 series. Exact set times and prices were not confirmed on a page I could load.
candidates.fit: Big melodic EDM outdoors in Greenpoint, which is the nostalgic Kygo-and-Gryffin corner of his library played loud. Lower stakes than a Mirage ticket, and it is done early.

candidates.title: Honey Dijon: Day & Night
candidates.time_text: 3pm to 5am; starts outdoors in The Ruins, ends in the Main Hall
candidates.summary: Honey Dijon takes over the entire Knockdown Center for fourteen hours, joined by Luke Solomon, Derrick Carter and Anastazja. It starts outside in The Ruins in the afternoon and finishes with her closing set in the Main Hall. 21+, tickets through RA and DICE; RA does not list a price.
candidates.fit: This is the daytime-into-night warehouse format he already loves from the BQE day party, with a genuine house legend instead of a festival headliner. He can show up at 4pm with the guys, get the daylight half, and bail before it turns into a 4am problem.

candidates.title: Mister Sunday Long Weekend Edition: Justin Carter and Eamon Harkin
candidates.summary: The founders of Nowadays play their own backyard for the Columbus Day weekend edition of their long-running outdoor Sunday party, 3pm to 9pm in the yard. Phones away on the dance floor is the house rule. Season tickets have been running $35 plus fee.
candidates.fit: Outdoor, daylight, ends at nine, and the crowd is grown adults who actually dance. It is the closest thing in the city to the BQE day party he loved, and it works whether he brings the guys or his wife.

candidates.title: The Nursery: Frank & Tony with Roman Flügel
candidates.summary: Public Records opens its outdoor plant nursery for a Sunday afternoon session with local deep-house duo Frank & Tony and German veteran Roman Flügel. Starts at 3pm in the open-air Nursery space in Gowanus. Ticketing is through Dice.
candidates.fit: Fifteen minutes from Fort Greene, best sound system in Brooklyn, and Roman Flügel is a Frankfurt lifer with thirty years of records behind him, which scratches the German itch without anybody dressing up. Small, outdoors, daytime.

candidates.title: Jan Blomqvist (live), Parallelle, Kanykei
candidates.summary: Berlin's Jan Blomqvist brings his live show to the Knockdown Center Main Hall on Friday Oct 16, with Parallelle and Kanykei supporting. Doors 10pm, runs to 4am; tickets on RA and DICE.
candidates.fit: Melodic house played live by a Berliner is the dead center of his library - Kalkbrenner-adjacent, Tinlicker-adjacent, and a real performance rather than a DJ on a laptop. Book it now, these sell.

candidates.title: Massano, Konstantin Sibold, SOEL
candidates.summary: Friday night at Knockdown Center with UK melodic techno producer Massano, German DJ Konstantin Sibold and SOEL. Listed on the venue's Dice page for Oct 23; set times and price were not confirmed on a page I could open.
candidates.fit: Massano is squarely in the Tinlicker and Rebūke lane he keeps in rotation, and Konstantin Sibold is a German house lifer. Worth checking the Dice page for price before the group chat.

candidates.title: Mala Junta: Yazzus / Akua / FASHION / DJ TOOL / Kilopatrah Jones
candidates.summary: Mala Junta, the Berlin party series born at ://about blank, brings its roster to BASEMENT for a Saturday night with Yazzus, Akua, FASHION, DJ TOOL, Kilopatrah Jones and Alfonso Javier. 10:30pm doors, two rooms.
candidates.fit: An actual Berlin party brand running a night in Queens, not an American club doing a Berlin theme. If he wants one proper late Saturday this month, this is the one.

candidates.title: 718 Sessions with Danny Krivit
candidates.summary: Danny Krivit's long-running 718 Sessions lands at Good Room on Sunday of the long weekend, with That Matt. Krivit has been doing this since the loft era; it is a dancing crowd, mostly over 35, classic New York disco and house.
candidates.fit: A genuine New York institution most people his age have never heard of, on a Sunday, at a human hour. Pair it with the Mister Sunday crowd if he wants a full long-weekend afternoon.

candidates.title: GENESI & Guests
candidates.time_text: evening into late night, extended set
candidates.summary: Italian house and techno producer GENESI gets an extended long-form set at Knockdown Center on Sunday Oct 11, billed as a deeper, slower-building session than his festival sets, with Welker also listed on the Dice page.
candidates.fit: Long-form sets from one DJ are where the melodic stuff he likes actually breathes, and Sunday of a three-day weekend is the one night he can go late without paying for it Monday.

candidates.title: Pretty Girl (DJ Set)
candidates.summary: Thursday night DJ set from Pretty Girl in The Atrium at Public Records, the restaurant-and-lounge side of the Gowanus campus, starting 10:30pm. Small room, serious sound system, food and drinks on site.
candidates.fit: The easy Thursday: twenty minutes from Fort Greene, eat first, stand next to the speakers in a room that holds a couple hundred people, home before it gets stupid.

candidates.title: AADJA, Kyle Geiger / Softi, DJ G / Zotos
candidates.summary: Friday night club program across all three Public Records rooms: AADJA and Kyle Geiger in the Sound Room, Softi and DJ G in The Atrium, Zotos upstairs. Doors 11pm.
candidates.fit: Three rooms, under a few hundred people total, the best listening-room sound in Brooklyn, and a ten-minute car ride home. This is his default Friday when nothing bigger is on.

candidates.title: ReSolute with Aurora Halal, Shvili and guests
candidates.summary: ReSolute, one of New York's oldest underground house and techno parties, runs a Friday night at H0L0 in Ridgewood with Aurora Halal and Shvili listed, tickets from $20. I could not load a primary organizer page to confirm the full lineup or set times.
candidates.fit: ReSolute is exactly the word-of-mouth, no-marketing-budget party he says he wants, and Aurora Halal is one of the better melodic-leaning DJs in the city. Verify on RA before committing.

candidates.title: CircoLoco New York (Halloween weekend)
candidates.summary: Teksupport brings the Ibiza party CircoLoco to the Navy Yard warehouse for two nights over Halloween weekend. Friday Oct 30: &ME, Rampa, Seth Troxler, Mochakk, Carlita, Beltran, Konstantin, Map.ache. Saturday Oct 31: Dixon, ANOTR, Jimi Jules, Aline Umber, Jamback, Krol, Rossi.
candidates.fit: The once-or-twice-a-year big warehouse night, on Halloween, fifteen minutes from his door, with Dixon and Rampa playing the melodic end of house rather than a bottle-service room. Buy early; Teksupport Saturdays sell out.

candidates.title: Elsewhere Halloween: Major League DJz, SAIDAH, D Stone
candidates.summary: Elsewhere's full-venue Halloween party is headlined by Major League DJz, the South African twins who built amapiano's global sound, with SAIDAH and D Stone. Doors 10:30pm, all rooms open, costumes expected.
candidates.fit: Amapiano is his current phase and Major League DJz are the actual source of it, not a bar DJ playing the hits. Costume night with the guys in Bushwick; this is a better Halloween than any party he will be invited to.

candidates.title: Mister Sunday: Floating Points and Justin Carter
candidates.time_text: 3pm to 9pm; Floating Points 6pm to 8pm, b2b to close
candidates.summary: Floating Points joins Justin Carter in the booth for the penultimate outdoor Mister Sunday of the season: Carter 3pm to 6pm, Floating Points 6pm to 8pm, the two back to back until 9pm. Outdoor yard at Nowadays.
candidates.fit: Floating Points is one of the few DJs who can play six hours of melodic music outdoors without it turning into a festival set, and it is over by nine. Nearly 2,000 people are already marked interested, so buy now.

candidates.title: Black Coffee
candidates.summary: South African producer Black Coffee plays the open-air Brooklyn Mirage on Saturday Oct 17, listed with a 10pm start. It is the only Mirage date currently showing on aggregator calendars for the rest of the season.
candidates.fit: Afro-house from the man who made it an export, in the biggest outdoor room in Brooklyn, and probably the last Mirage night of the year. It is a spectacle night, which he budgets for a few times a year.

candidates.title: Mark Broom, Julia Govor / Blue Hour, Neel / Yasmeenah
candidates.summary: Halloween-weekend Friday across all three Public Records rooms: UK techno veteran Mark Broom with Julia Govor in the Sound Room, Blue Hour and Neel in The Atrium, Yasmeenah upstairs. 11pm doors.
candidates.fit: If CircoLoco feels too big, this is the same weekend done properly small: three rooms, real techno bookings, twenty minutes from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: DURATIONS: Dasha Rush, Blue Hour, Claudio PRC & Francis Harris
candidates.summary: The club night inside Public Records' DURATIONS festival (Nov 9 to 15), with Berlin-based Dasha Rush, Decoder and Innersha live in the Sound Room, Human Space Machine, Claudio PRC and Francis Harris in The Atrium, Afrikan Sciences upstairs. Festival also includes Suzanne Ciani and DJ Sprinkles on other nights.
candidates.fit: A week-long festival run by one venue, programmed for people who care about sound rather than lineup posters. Dasha Rush is a Berlin techno artist in a 200-person room, which is his stated sweet spot exactly.

candidates.title: The Lot Radio
candidates.time_text: daytime into evening, sets most days
candidates.summary: Independent radio station broadcasting from a shipping container on a triangle of asphalt in Greenpoint, with DJs playing live to a small outdoor crowd and a coffee and beer window. Free to stand there. I could not load the schedule page this week, so check the site for who is on before going.
candidates.fit: This is the permanent version of the BQE day party he loved: outdoor, free, forty people, a DJ you have never heard of playing something good. Good default for a Saturday afternoon when nothing is booked, and fine with a stroller.

candidates.title: Polymarket UFC 334: Gane vs. Hokit
candidates.summary: UFC's annual New York pay-per-view lands at the Garden on Saturday, November 14. Ciryl Gane defends the heavyweight title against Josh Hokit, and Kayla Harrison vs. Amanda Nunes for the women's bantamweight belt is the co-main; Caio Borralho vs. Yousri Belgaroui sits under it. Tickets went on public sale September 25 through Ticketmaster and the card page lists main card at 9pm ET.
candidates.fit: This is the once-or-twice-a-year big spectacle he budgets for: a real UFC numbered card at MSG with two title fights, exactly the kind of night he'd organize three friends around. He trains Muay Thai and teaches Krav Maga, so a heavyweight title fight at the Garden is his version of the Kx5 show.

candidates.title: Knicks Ring Night: New York Knicks vs. Philadelphia 76ers
candidates.summary: The Knicks raise their championship banner and collect their rings before opening the season against Philadelphia on Tuesday, October 20 at Madison Square Garden. Reporting on the NBA's schedule release has the ceremony at 6:30pm and tip at 7pm, with LeBron James making his 76ers debut. Tickets are through Ticketmaster.
candidates.fit: He spent the playoff run watching this team in bars with the guys. This is the payoff night, and it is the one regular-season Knicks ticket worth breaking his no-Tuesday rule for. If the Garden is out of reach, it's also the week's best excuse to lock a table somewhere in Fort Greene early.

candidates.title: New York Liberty vs. Atlanta Dream — WNBA Semifinals, Game 3
candidates.summary: Game 3 of the WNBA semifinal series between the Liberty and the Atlanta Dream, Friday October 9 at Barclays Center. The arena's own event calendar lists it; tip-off time was not posted on the calendar page at the time of writing. Tickets through Ticketmaster via the Barclays event page.
candidates.fit: Playoff basketball he can walk to from Fort Greene, in a loud building, on a Friday night. He doesn't buy regular-season tickets, but a semifinal elimination-stakes game in his front yard is exactly the category he does show up for.

candidates.title: BKFC 95: Herring vs. Dodson
candidates.summary: Bare Knuckle Fighting Championship brings BKFC 95: Herring vs. Dodson to the Prudential Center on Saturday, October 17 at 8pm, per the arena's own event calendar. Tickets are sold through Ticketmaster off the venue page. It's a PATH ride from Manhattan.
candidates.fit: A real pro card, a short train away, and bare-knuckle is the kind of thing his Kings Combat crew will have opinions about. Smaller and nastier than a UFC night, which is the point.

candidates.title: New York Liberty vs. Atlanta Dream — WNBA Semifinals, Game 5 (if necessary)
candidates.summary: A potential Game 5 of the Liberty–Dream semifinal series, Sunday October 11 at Barclays Center, listed on the arena calendar as 'if necessary.' It only happens if the series goes the distance. Tip-off time was not posted on the calendar page.
candidates.fit: If the series goes five, this is a win-or-go-home game ten minutes from his door on a Sunday. Worth holding the afternoon loosely and deciding Saturday night.

candidates.title: Canelo Álvarez vs. Christian Mbilli (WBC super middleweight title, DAZN PPV)
candidates.summary: Canelo's comeback fight against undefeated WBC super middleweight champion Christian Mbilli is officially set for Saturday, October 31 in Riyadh, airing on DAZN pay-per-view. The WBC and Ring Magazine both confirmed date and venue after the fight was moved from September 12. No undercard was confirmed as of the announcement.
candidates.fit: The biggest boxing PPV of the fall lands on Halloween night, which means it's either a reason to skip the costume party or the thing playing behind one. He'll want to know the date now so he can plan around it rather than find out the morning after.

candidates.title: WWE: RAW & SmackDown — Two Shows, One Night
candidates.summary: WWE runs both RAW and SmackDown back to back in a single Barclays Center ticket on Monday, November 2, per the arena's event page. One admission covers both broadcasts. Tickets are through Ticketmaster off the venue listing.
candidates.fit: He already likes live pro wrestling as a bar format; this is the full-volume arena version, walkable from Fort Greene, and a double broadcast in one night is the sort of oddity worth dragging two friends to. It's a Monday, so it only clears his bar because it's a one-off.

candidates.title: NBA Preseason: New York Knicks vs. Washington Wizards
candidates.summary: The Knicks host Washington in a preseason game at Madison Square Garden on Thursday, October 8 at 7:30pm, listed on the official Knicks Ticketmaster schedule. Preseason tickets are the cheapest Garden basketball of the year. Starters frequently sit in preseason, so treat it as a cheap first look, not a marquee game.
candidates.fit: It's his Thursday slot, it's his team, and it's the first Garden night of a championship-defense season for the price of a dinner. Low stakes, easy to get three guys to say yes.

candidates.title: UFC Fight Night: Allen vs. Duncan (Paramount+)
candidates.summary: Top-ten middleweights Brendan Allen and Christian Leroy Duncan headline a UFC Fight Night from the APEX on Saturday, October 10, with prelims at 5pm ET and the main card at 8pm ET on Paramount+. No live NYC component — this is a watch-it card. Loopy Godinez, Andre Fili and Gerald Meerschaert are also on it.
candidates.fit: A striker-heavy middleweight main event is the sort of card his gym crew will actually break down afterward, and an 8pm start means it's over at a dad-reasonable hour. Good filler for a Saturday where the plan is beers and a screen rather than a ticket.

candidates.title: Oktoberfest Close Out at Black Forest Brooklyn (Fort Greene)
candidates.price_text: around $15 entry; kids under 10 free (2025 pricing — confirm)
candidates.summary: The final session of Black Forest's 2026 Oktoberfest run, listed on Resy for Saturday October 24 at 1pm at the Fort Greene location. Live oompah band, German food, costume contest. The restaurant's Oktoberfest sessions are explicitly family-friendly with kids under 10 admitted free.
candidates.fit: A daytime German party with live brass, four blocks from home, where a 1-year-old who already listens to German kids' songs can be loud without anyone caring — and the adults get a proper Maß. Done well before nap-time collapse.

candidates.title: Red Hook Lobster Pound truck at Strong Rope Brewery
candidates.summary: Strong Rope's own events calendar lists the Red Hook Lobster Pound truck parked at the brewery on Sunday, October 11, serving lobster rolls alongside their all-New-York-grain beer. Strong Rope runs two taprooms (Red Hook and Gowanus) and the calendar entry does not name which one, so confirm on the event page before you go. No ticket, no cover; you pay for beer and rolls.
candidates.fit: Strong Rope on a sunny day is already one of his favorite afternoons in the city, and this is the same hang with a reason to show up. Weekend daytime, stroller-tolerant, and done by mid-afternoon if he brings the kid.

candidates.title: Booth's Extra Fine opens in Williamsburg
candidates.summary: A vintage-styled Williamsburg steakhouse named after an owner's grandfather, doing broiled steaks, chilled seafood towers and very cold martinis. The Infatuation's fall openings guide lists the opening date as October 6, 2026 at 62 S 2nd St. Per-person spend is not published yet; assume steakhouse money.
candidates.fit: He did a boys' night at Keens and loved it. This is the brand-new, nobody-has-been-yet version of that, in the neighborhood where he already trains, before anyone has written it up properly.

candidates.title: Limousine, new cocktail bar with a private karaoke room
candidates.summary: From the team behind Five Leaves and Goldie's, Limousine took over the old Ponyboy space in Greenpoint: black banquettes, a proper cocktail list, deviled eggs and mortadella skewers served until midnight, and a private karaoke room you can rent. Listed in The Infatuation's new-openings guide as of October 1, 2026. Room rental pricing is not published.
candidates.fit: A dark Brooklyn cocktail bar with a bookable karaoke room is a plan, not a 'grab a drink' text. Four guys, a room, and nobody waiting in line.

candidates.title: Cmarty's Jerk pop-up inside King Tai
candidates.summary: A Jamaican-American jerk pop-up running out of the kitchen at King Tai, a small Crown Heights bar doing tiki without the kitsch. The menu rotates on the cook's whim: jerk banh mi, jerk quesadillas, bourbon wings, pork shu mai. You order off a QR code at the table and they bring it out. Still listed on The Infatuation's Crown Heights page as of July 2026, but the hours come from an older pop-ups guide, so check their Instagram before you commit.
candidates.fit: Restaurant-inside-a-bar is exactly the format he likes, it's a Thursday-night walk from Fort Greene, and it scratches the Caribbean-Brooklyn itch that his listening habits say he's deep in right now.

candidates.title: Oktoberfest Close-Out Party at Black Forest Brooklyn (Smith St)
candidates.price_text: $33 per person on Resy, includes your first 1-liter beer
candidates.summary: The last of the six Oktoberfest Saturdays, at the Smith Street location. The Resy venue page lists it as 'Oktoberfest Close-Out,' Saturday October 24 at 4pm, with an earlier Smith Street Oktoberfest on October 17 at 7pm. Same format as Fort Greene: oompah band, liter steins, costume and stein-holding contests, $33 per person including the first beer.
candidates.fit: If October 10 sells out or he wants the afternoon version instead of the night version, this is the backup, and the close-out is always the rowdiest of the six. Book it now; these tables go.

candidates.title: Meat Asia Asian BBQ pop-up at Strong Rope Brewery
candidates.summary: Strong Rope's calendar has Meat Asia serving Asian barbecue at the brewery on Friday, October 23. It's a walk-in food pop-up inside the taproom, no ticket. As with their other food dates, the calendar doesn't specify Red Hook versus Gowanus, so check the event page. Note that the Red Hook taproom is closed all day October 16 for a private event.
candidates.fit: Barbecue and beer with two friends at a brewery he already rates, on a Friday, with no reservation to chase. Low effort, high hit rate.

candidates.title: SWEETS by Odo, October dessert pop-up
candidates.summary: Odo, the Japanese kaiseki counter, runs a monthly dessert-only pop-up curated by chef Hiroki Odo and led by executive pastry chef Yoshie Nakanishi. The October edition is Saturday October 17 and Sunday October 18, 2026, with multiple seatings, ticketed through Tock at $97 per person.
candidates.fit: A seated, chef-driven, two-days-only thing in a small room is more his register than a wine festival. Good date night with his wife: short, specific, and nobody they know will have done it.

candidates.title: Yoshino five-year anniversary menu
candidates.summary: Resy's Hit List flags that Michelin-starred Yoshino is running a one-off anniversary omakase from September 29 through October 10, 2026, built around chef Tadashi 'Edowan' Yoshida's career. It is a counter, so it is a two-person plan, not a group one. Price is not published in the listing; this is a genuine splurge.
candidates.fit: He'll pay for special, and this is a limited-run menu at a serious counter rather than a hyped opening. Last night of the run is Saturday October 10, so it's book-tonight-or-forget-it.

candidates.title: FAD Market at Brooklyn Brewery
candidates.summary: FAD Market, the independent fashion, art and design pop-up marketplace, sets up inside Brooklyn Brewery on October 17 and 18, 2026, as part of a run of fall markets (Empire Stores in Dumbo Oct 3-4, St. Paul in Cobble Hill Oct 24-25). Admission details and hours were not confirmed on an organizer page.
candidates.fit: A design market inside a brewery is the weekend-daytime version of his sunny-day brewery hang, and it's the kind of small-maker thing he likes more than a food festival. Works with the stroller.

candidates.title: The Cervantes Room at El Quijote
candidates.summary: Resy's New York events feed lists the Cervantes Room at El Quijote, the old Spanish dining room in the Hotel Chelsea, as a bookable nightly experience running 5pm to 10:30pm. It reads as a separate reservable room rather than a regular table, which makes it a candidate for a six-to-eight-person group dinner. Menu format and per-person cost were not confirmed on the restaurant's own page.
candidates.fit: He wants big shared-table meals for a group, and a private-feeling room inside a 1930s Spanish dining room beats another steakhouse booking. Call them before promising the group chat anything.

candidates.title: LIPS: Rocky Horror
candidates.summary: House of Yes stages Rocky Horror live, reimagined and performed by its own cast rather than screened with a shadow cast. Thursday Oct 8 (6:30pm doors) and Friday Oct 9 are both on; there is another date Thursday Oct 22 if those sell out. Tickets run roughly $52-$58 on Shotgun, with reserved tables available.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for Rocky Horror in Flatbush and loved it; this is the same ritual with House of Yes production value, in Bushwick, on a Thursday. Costume encouraged, virgins welcome, and it is over by 9:30 so he is home at a dad-reasonable hour.

candidates.title: Petite Rouge
candidates.time_text: Thu, Fri, Sat 8pm; Sun 6pm; about 90 minutes with an intermission
candidates.price_text: $35 to $49 depending on the night, before champagne upgrades
candidates.summary: Company XIV's current mainstage show is Petite Rouge, Austin McCormick's baroque-burlesque Little Red Riding Hood, and the company site says it has been extended through Halloween. Performances are Thursday through Saturday at 8pm and Sunday at 6pm at Théâtre XIV in Bushwick, 21+. Seats start around $35 midweek and $45 on weekends, plus the usual champagne-couch upgrades.
candidates.fit: Company XIV is his favorite room in the city and their Halloween show was a highlight, so catching the last three weekends of Petite Rouge before it closes Oct 31 is the obvious date night. Book a champagne couch and it is a proper occasion, not a night out.

candidates.title: Halloween 13 3/4: Strip of the Slasher Movie Villains
candidates.summary: A guest burlesque production at the Slipper Room built entirely around slasher-movie villains, listed on the venue calendar for Thursday Oct 8 at 7pm. The Slipper Room has been doing comedy, sideshow, magic and burlesque in the same small Orchard Street room since 1999. Sir Richard Castle's Naughty Little Show follows at 9:30pm the same night if you want to stay.
candidates.fit: Small-room burlesque with a costume-horror conceit, on his main weeknight slot, in exactly the register of the Company XIV Halloween show he loved. Two shows back to back in one room makes it an easy plan to hand the guys.

candidates.title: New York City Ballet: Masters at Work I
candidates.time_text: evening performances both nights, about 2 hours 10 minutes
candidates.address: 20 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023
candidates.summary: Three Balanchine and Robbins works in one evening: La Source, The Four Temperaments, and Robbins' comic The Concert, played with the pianist onstage. NYCB lists this program on Oct 9 and Oct 10 evening, the last two outings before the fall season closes Oct 18. Runs about two hours ten minutes at the Koch Theater.
candidates.fit: The Nutcracker at Lincoln Center is his favorite night in the city, and this is the same company, same house, on a Friday or Saturday night without waiting for December. The Concert is genuinely funny, which makes it an easier sell than a straight abstract program.

candidates.title: The Third Eye: Olivia Harrison in conversation with Martin Scorsese
candidates.summary: BAM hosts Olivia Harrison in conversation with Martin Scorsese on Tuesday Oct 6 as part of its October program. Tickets through bam.org.
candidates.fit: A Tuesday only clears his bar if the speaker is a genuine heavyweight, and Scorsese sitting down ten minutes from his apartment qualifies. Likely to be close to sold out, so he'd need to move today.

candidates.title: A Brooklyn Dream: cinema experience with Kaves Q&A
candidates.summary: Michael 'Kaves' McLeer, the Brooklyn artist, musician and filmmaker behind the immersive production A Brooklyn Dream, brings the next phase of the project to Nitehawk Prospect Park as a cinema experience on Thursday Oct 8 at 7pm, followed by a Q&A with him. Nitehawk is a dine-in theater, so dinner happens in your seat.
candidates.fit: This is the deep-Brooklyn, had-to-know-about-it register he asks for: a local artist's long-running immersive project, a real room, and the director in it answering questions. Thursday night, one subway stop past Prospect Heights.

candidates.title: Cold Plunge with Kurt Braunohler
candidates.summary: Kurt Braunohler's recurring Union Hall show, this edition with Kristen Schaal, Phoebe Robinson, Jordan Doll and Ike Ufomadu. Wednesday Oct 7, 7:30pm, in Union Hall's basement room, which holds under 200 people. The series returns Nov 4 if this date doesn't work.
candidates.fit: That is a genuinely stacked lineup for a basement bar room, and it is the kind of booking you only find by reading the venue calendar rather than a listicle. Midweek, but the lineup justifies it.

candidates.title: The George Lucas Talk Show
candidates.summary: The long-running cult live talk show in which a 'retired filmmaker George Lucas' interviews real guests alongside his sidekick Watto, hosted by Connor Ratliff and produced by Patrick Cotnoir. Thursday Oct 8 at Littlefield, doors 7pm, show 8pm, 21+. Guests are announced close to showtime.
candidates.fit: Pure word-of-mouth comedy with a committed bit, in a mid-size Gowanus room rather than a club with a two-drink minimum. Easy Thursday with one or two friends, and Parklife next door after.

candidates.title: Hack City Comedy with Mic Nguyen and Jenny Arimoto
candidates.summary: Union Hall's long-running Hack City showcase, this Friday with Aparna Nancherla, Sabrina Wu, Hanna Dickinson and Julio Diaz. Friday Oct 9, 7:30pm, downstairs at Union Hall. Early enough that the night is still young afterward.
candidates.fit: Small basement room, four names who all sell out bigger rooms elsewhere, and a 7:30 start that leaves time for a drink after. This is the format he already likes better than a comedy club.

candidates.title: Mr. Choade's Upstairs Downstairs
candidates.summary: The Slipper Room's Saturday-night variety showcase, a mix of burlesque, sideshow, magic and comedy hosted in character. Saturday Oct 10 at 8pm on the venue calendar. The room is small and the show is deliberately chaotic.
candidates.fit: Old-school New York variety in a 1999-vintage Orchard Street room, the kind of oddball cabaret he goes for with the guys. Saturday night, Manhattan, zero tourist-core energy.

candidates.title: Molly Kearney & Friends
candidates.summary: Former SNL cast member Molly Kearney headlines a friends-and-guests night at the Bell House on Thursday Oct 8 at 7:30pm. Guest comics are typically announced late or kept as a surprise. The Bell House is a converted Gowanus warehouse with a front bar you can hang in before and after.
candidates.fit: A Thursday alternative to the Littlefield show, three blocks away, with the loose drop-in lineup format he liked about that Midtown apartment show. Big enough room that you can show up with four people without pre-planning seats.

candidates.title: Karaoke Tremendous
candidates.time_text: starts just before midnight, runs late
candidates.price_text: listed as a free registration on Eventbrite
candidates.summary: Union Hall's late-night karaoke takes over the downstairs room most Fridays at 11:59pm, listed on Eventbrite as a free RSVP rather than a paid ticket. It runs again Oct 16, Oct 23, Oct 30 and Nov 6. No private room, no booking fee, just a basement and a signup sheet.
candidates.fit: He already gets on stage for things, and this is the cheap second half of a Union Hall night if he books the 7:30 comedy show first. One ticket link, two parts of the evening, no second plan required.

candidates.title: Heel Toe Rodeo: beginner line dancing
candidates.summary: A beginner-friendly line dancing night at Littlefield with lessons taught throughout the evening, 21+, Tuesday Oct 6 from 7:30 to 10:30pm. It is a recurring Littlefield series rather than a one-off.
candidates.fit: Interactive, country-soundtracked, and nobody is good at it, which is the whole point; it sits right next to the Luke Combs and Florida Georgia Line streak in his library. A Tuesday, so file it as a backup rather than the headline plan.

candidates.title: The Slipper Room Show + Midnight Show
candidates.summary: The house show on Friday Oct 9 at 8pm, with a separate later edition at 10:45pm that runs dirtier and looser. Burlesque, sideshow and magic acts rotate weekly. Both are on the venue's own calendar.
candidates.fit: If the Thursday slasher-burlesque night doesn't land, this is the same room on a Friday with the late show as the real draw. Small, seedy in the good way, and nothing about it reads as a listicle pick.

candidates.title: Nutcracker Rouge
candidates.price_text: from about $35 on weeknights, $39 on weekends
candidates.summary: Company XIV's holiday signature returns to Théâtre XIV on Nov 12 and runs through the winter. It is Tchaikovsky by way of aerial circus, opera singers and burlesque, 21+ only. Tickets are on sale now and the company is running a presale off its own site.
candidates.fit: He has the actual Nutcracker scores in his library and Company XIV is his favorite room; this is both at once, and the good seats for the December weekends go first. Book it in October, not November.

candidates.title: City of Gods Halloween Festival 2026
candidates.summary: House of Yes takes over Industry City for its eighth City of Gods, described on their calendar as two nights of costumed, heavily produced Halloween spectacle. Friday Oct 23 doors at 9pm; the listing refers to a second night but I only confirmed the Friday date. Tables are bookable through House of Yes.
candidates.fit: This is the once-in-a-while big spectacle slot: warehouse scale, serious costume culture, House of Yes production, and a DJ lineup rather than a bottle-service room. The closest thing in the fall calendar to that day party by the BQE, scaled up.

candidates.title: Halloween Night: comedians in costume, in character
candidates.summary: On Halloween night Littlefield puts comedians on stage in costume performing their sets entirely in character, hosted by Brittany Carney with Ike Ufomadu, Jenny Zigrino, Neel Ghosh, Shaunak Gokhale, Don Will and others. There is an audience costume contest with prizes. Doors 6:30pm, show 7:30pm, announced on the venue's own channels.
candidates.fit: Costume night with an actual format instead of just a bar in wigs, and he participates by dressing up rather than watching. Early enough on Halloween that it can be the first stop rather than the whole night.

candidates.title: American Ballet Theatre Fall Season
candidates.time_text: evenings and matinees across the run
candidates.address: 20 Lincoln Center Plaza, New York, NY 10023
candidates.summary: ABT takes over the Koch Theater from Oct 21 to 31 with three repertory programs including a world premiere and company premieres. It is a short eleven-day season that moves in right after NYCB's fall run ends. Programming details are on ABT's own announcement.
candidates.fit: The second half of the Lincoln Center date-night option, and a shorter window than NYCB, so it needs booking in advance. Good fallback if the Oct 9 and 10 NYCB nights don't work.

candidates.title: Brett Goldstein Runs His Hour Before His Tour
candidates.summary: Brett Goldstein works out his full hour at the Bell House on Wednesday Oct 21 at 7:30pm before taking it on the road. It is a warehouse room in Gowanus, not an arena, and these work-in-progress dates tend to go fast.
candidates.fit: The exact opposite of the big-arena comedian he has no interest in: same performer, 500-cap room, material that is still being figured out. A Wednesday, so only worth it because of the room.

candidates.title: The Roundup with DJ Cowboy
candidates.price_text: listed as a free registration on Eventbrite
candidates.summary: A late-night country dance party in Union Hall's basement, Saturday Oct 24 starting at 11:59pm, listed as a free RSVP. It runs as an occasional series rather than every week.
candidates.fit: The country lane in his library is real and underserved, and this is a basement full of people taking it half-seriously rather than a themed bar with a mechanical bull. Free, late, and a short cab from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: The Moth StorySLAM
candidates.summary: The Moth's open-draw storytelling competition at the Bell House on Tuesday Oct 13 at 8pm. Anyone can put their name in the hat on the night and ten names get pulled; the audience judges. Theme is announced in advance by The Moth.
candidates.fit: Interactive in the way he actually wants: he can put his own name in the hat and get five minutes on a real stage. A Tuesday, so it only works if he is feeling it, but it is the cheapest route to participating rather than watching.

candidates.title: Hewa Rwanda - Letter to the absent
candidates.summary: Dorcy Rugamba adapts his memoir dedicated to the family he lost in the Rwandan genocide into a theatrical piece performed alongside guitarist Majnun, part of BAM's Next Wave festival. Oct 7 to 11 at BAM in Fort Greene. It is the opening week of Next Wave 2026.
candidates.fit: Serious Next Wave programming at the institution he can walk to, and a counterweight to a month of burlesque and costume nights. Heavy material, so it is a date night only if that is the mood.

candidates.title: The Tiny Cupboard
candidates.time_text: shows nightly; Sun–Thu typically 8pm & 9:30pm (plus 11pm open mic), Fri/Sat 7pm, 8:30pm & 10:15pm
candidates.price_text: $13.50 + $2.41 fee online Sun–Thu ($20 at the door); Fri/Sat shows $19.50 + $2.82 fee online, $25 at the door
candidates.summary: A community-built indie stand-up club in Bushwick with a rooftop room, a small indoor room, and a board game and video game bar behind it. Shows run every single night, one ticket covers multiple lineups, there is no drink minimum, and tickets are $13.50 online. Free karaoke runs in the game bar on some nights.
candidates.fit: No marketing budget, no bringer shows, no barkers, and a room small enough that you can talk to the comics afterward; this is the standing answer when he wants a plan in Bushwick with 48 hours' notice. The game bar out back means the night keeps going without a second venue.

candidates.title: Beat Drop: DJ Takeover ft. Anil + Friends
candidates.summary: Othership's Williamsburg sauna turns into a dance floor for a live DJ takeover: three hours of louder music, towel waving, aromatherapy and ice baths between rounds. Saturday Oct 10, 9pm to midnight. Sober-curious, no bar, booked by the session so the room stays small.
candidates.fit: This is the overlap of two things he already loves: a full bathhouse day with a friend, and a DJ who actually plays. It's a Saturday night out with the guys that doesn't need a 2am set or a bottle minimum, and it's in Williamsburg where he already trains.

candidates.title: Deep Listening Night: RÜFÜS DU SOL
candidates.summary: One night, one catalog: the whole Othership Flatiron sound system is given over to RÜFÜS DU SOL, start to finish, with sauna rounds, ice baths, towel waving and aromatherapy. Friday Oct 9, 9pm to 11:30pm. Booked as a timed session, so capacity is small.
candidates.fit: Melodic house with real low end is his core lane, and this is that sound played loud in a 185-degree room instead of a club. It's a Friday night he can do sober, get home from, and still feel like he did something.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Atlantic Avenue day pass
candidates.time_text: open daily, long hours; day pass is untimed so you can stay all day
candidates.price_text: day pass from $29, price varies by day and time
candidates.summary: Bathhouse's third NYC location opened in May 2026 on Atlantic Avenue, a few blocks from Barclays Center. Three thermal pools (104F hot, 98F neutral, 50F plunge), a 194F banya, an infrared sauna, and a 100-plus-seat event sauna that runs free daily Aufguss ceremonies. Day passes start at $29 and are untimed.
candidates.fit: The Russian bathhouse day with a friend is one of his favorite things he's ever done here, and this is the same format fifteen minutes from his door in Fort Greene. The 100-seat event sauna with live Aufguss is the closest thing New York has to a performance you sweat through.

candidates.title: Couples Night (Guided You + Me: Relationship)
candidates.summary: A guided sauna and ice bath session built for two, led by an Othership facilitator who paces the hot and cold rounds for couples. Saturday Oct 10 at the Flatiron location. Also running the same night in Toronto, so book the Flatiron listing specifically.
candidates.fit: A babysitter-night that isn't dinner and a cocktail. Same contrast-therapy thing he already likes, but guided and made for two, and it's done early enough to still grab a drink after.

candidates.title: Beat Drop: DJ Takeover
candidates.summary: The Flatiron edition of Othership's live-DJ sauna night: two hours of louder music, towel waving, ice baths and dancing in the heat. Saturday Oct 17. Sessions sell out, so it's a book-ahead.
candidates.fit: Backup slot if Oct 10 in Williamsburg doesn't work for the crew. Same premise, Manhattan side, and Flatiron is an easy meet point if one of the guys is coming from the city.

candidates.title: Runners' Night x Vivobarefoot
candidates.time_text: evening; group run first, then sauna and ice
candidates.summary: A group run out of Othership Williamsburg with Vivobarefoot, followed by heat, cold plunge and breathwork back at the studio. Tuesday Oct 13. One organizer, one route, a fixed end point.
candidates.fit: This is the anti-run-club run club: there's an actual destination and a sauna at the end, not a bar and a group chat. Good three weeks out from marathon week if he wants legs under him, and it's a Tuesday so it's a radar item, not a main pick.

candidates.title: Friend[ship]: A Guided Social
candidates.summary: A facilitated hot-and-cold social at Othership Williamsburg built around meeting people through the rounds rather than small talk at a bar. Monday Oct 12.
candidates.fit: Worth flagging only because he wants to be the guy with the plan: this is a thing you drag one friend to and come out having talked to strangers. Monday night, so strictly radar unless the week is empty.

candidates.title: Candlelit Restorative Free Flow
candidates.summary: A 75-minute candlelit session at Othership Williamsburg with the lights down and the programming built entirely around rest: slow sauna rounds, quiet music, ice bath when you want it. Sunday Oct 18.
candidates.fit: The quiet counterweight to the DJ nights, and a good Sunday-afternoon-into-evening move with his wife when the sitter window is short. Same room he'd go to anyway, run at a completely different tempo.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Bathhouse
candidates.time_text: open daily from 9am; midnight close on Fridays and Saturdays
candidates.summary: A small independent bathhouse on Flatbush Avenue with three saunas, three tubs including a cold plunge, and an attached performance space called the Whole Picture Theatre. They periodically run 'Brooklyn Bathhouse at Night' sessions with local DJs, live music and a mocktail included, ticketed through Eventbrite and listed on Resident Advisor.
candidates.fit: This is the un-marketed version of the thing he likes: no membership tier, no wellness branding, a theater bolted onto a sauna in Flatbush. Worth getting on their Eventbrite list now so he catches the next DJ night before it's on anyone's radar.

candidates.title: Lore Bathing Club
candidates.summary: A contrast-therapy club in NoHo with a 15-person infrared sauna, an alder-wood Finnish sauna, a cold plunge and heated clay benches. It opened members-only and now takes public bookings in 75-minute slots, with a strict no-phones policy.
candidates.fit: Fifteen people in the sauna and phones banned is about as close to 'you had to know someone' as bathing gets in Manhattan. Good for a two-man session before dinner downtown rather than a full-day thing.

candidates.title: Bike MS: New York City 2026
candidates.summary: The National MS Society's New York City ride on Sunday Oct 18, 2026, with 30-mile and 50-mile route options through the city. Registration carries a $250 fundraising minimum rather than a flat entry fee.
candidates.fit: He rode Lower Manhattan to the GW Bridge with friends and loved it, and this is that distance with a closed route, rest stops and a reason to get three guys out of bed on a Sunday. Needs sign-up ahead of time, so it's a radar item.

candidates.title: Too Much Is Better Than Too Little: Alfred Hilsberg, ZickZack & the Invention of the German Underground
candidates.time_text: opening reception Thu Oct 8, 6-8pm; gallery hours Thursday-Sunday 3-8pm
candidates.summary: The first show ever mounted outside Germany about Alfred Hilsberg and ZickZack, the Hamburg label behind Einstürzende Neubauten, Palais Schaumburg and the Neue Deutsche Welle underground. Rare records, badges, flyers, posters, photography and early Super-8, in a small Lower East Side gallery, presented by Goethe-Institut New York as part of its Punk@50 series. Goethe lists the run as October 8 to November 7; CUNY's weekly lecture listing puts a Sukhdev Sandhu talk of the same title at 19 Essex Street at 6pm during the October 5–11 week, which lines up with an October 8 opening.
candidates.fit: German music history in a room you could cross in ten steps, run by a cultural institute with no marketing budget — exactly the 'secret you had to know about' register, and it's the deep end of the Berlin/German lane he already lives in.

candidates.title: European Literature Night 2026
candidates.summary: An evening festival of European writers hosted across the rooms of the Ukrainian Institute's Fifth Avenue Beaux-Arts mansion, Wednesday October 28, 6 to 10pm, co-organized by the European cultural institutes including Goethe-Institut New York. Listed on the Goethe-Institut New York calendar.
candidates.fit: It's a Wednesday, so only if the building itself sells it — the Fletcher-Sinclair mansion is the kind of place you otherwise only get into during Open House New York. More of a wander-with-a-drink evening than a reading series.

candidates.title: German Tape Delinquents: Rise of the German Home Recording Tape Scene, 1980–1990, feat. Felix Kubin
candidates.summary: Talk on Germany's 1980s cassette underground featuring Felix Kubin, the Hamburg electronic composer and Gagarin label founder who has been making dadaist synth music since he was a teenager with a tape deck. Tuesday October 13, 6:30 to 8:30pm at Various/Artists on Essex Street, part of Goethe-Institut New York's Punk@50 series.
candidates.fit: It's a Tuesday, so it has to earn it: Felix Kubin in a Lower East Side gallery talking about German bedroom electronics is a one-night, know-someone-to-know-about-it thing, and it sits right between his German lane and his electronic-music lane.

candidates.title: Zombie Films: German Halloween Double Feature
candidates.summary: The German Film Office programs a Halloween-week double feature of German zombie favorites, including the splatter cult item German Chainsaw Massacre, at the Goethe-Institut on Irving Place. Thursday October 29, 7 to 10pm. Listed on the German Film Office calendar.
candidates.fit: Halloween week, German, and gleefully stupid in the right way — this is the costume-screening lane (he dressed up for Rocky Horror in Flatbush) without the line-culture crowd, and it lands on a Thursday.

candidates.title: Rabih Mroué & Lina Majdalanie: Four Walls and a Roof (North American premiere)
candidates.summary: North American premiere of a lecture-performance by Beirut-born, Berlin-based artists Rabih Mroué and Lina Majdalanie, co-presented by Goethe-Institut New York at NYU Skirball, October 22 to 24, 2026. Listed on the Goethe-Institut New York events calendar.
candidates.fit: Not generic theater — it's documentary-performance from two Berlin-based artists, the kind of thing that plays three nights and then is gone. Thursday Oct 22 fits his weeknight slot; good date night if she's up for something demanding.

candidates.title: Fall Festival at Lakeside, Prospect Park
candidates.time_text: weekends from 11am; go in the late morning
candidates.price_text: varies by activity — check the Lakeside page
candidates.summary: A month-long fall takeover of the LeFrak Center in Prospect Park running October 8 through November 1, 2026: pumpkins, hay bales, carnival games, seasonal food, photo stations and a haunted-hotel walkthrough for older kids. Weekends run 11am to 10pm per the Prospect Park Alliance listing. Flat, paved, stroller-friendly, and a short ride from Fort Greene.
candidates.fit: The family pick that doesn't require a car or a train: stroller rolls straight in, the 1-year-old gets pumpkins and a carousel-adjacent scene, and you're out by early afternoon. Skip the haunted hotel.

candidates.title: Marlon James: The Disappearers
candidates.summary: Booker Prize winner Marlon James in conversation at Pioneer Works, Sunday October 11 at 4pm, per CUNY's weekly New York lecture listing. Pioneer Works is the converted ironworks on Pioneer Street in Red Hook; its talks run in the main hall and are usually ticketed cheap or free with RSVP.
candidates.fit: Red Hook is on his list, Pioneer Works is the right kind of room, and a Sunday-afternoon slot fits the weekend-daytime window. Pair it with Strong Rope afterwards — he already likes that corner of the city on a clear day.

candidates.title: Manual Cinema: The 4th Witch
candidates.summary: Chicago's Emmy-winning Manual Cinema builds live shadow-puppet films in front of you — overhead projectors, paper cutouts, live actors and a live score, assembled in real time. The 4th Witch is a wordless Macbeth-adjacent fable. NYU's calendar lists performances October 15 to 17, 2026, with a Saturday 3pm and 7:30pm.
candidates.fit: Company XIV taste, different medium: a small handmade spectacle where you watch the machinery working, not a Broadway product. Good date night, and the Saturday matinee is an option if the sitter falls through.

candidates.title: St. Martin's Lantern Walk in Prospect Park (CityKinder)
candidates.time_text: late afternoon, at dusk — 2026 date not yet posted
candidates.summary: CityKinder, the German-speaking family network in New York, runs an annual Laternenlauf in Prospect Park every November: families gather at dusk with handmade lanterns, sing the traditional songs, then process through the park to a reenactment of St. Martin on horseback sharing his cloak. CityKinder's event page is live but the 2026 date was not posted when I checked — it typically lands on a weekend near November 11.
candidates.fit: This is the single best family pick of the season for him: German-language, community-run, no marketing, and the 1-year-old who already gets Lichterkinder lantern songs at home gets to carry one. Watch CityKinder's page and put it on the calendar the day it drops.

candidates.title: Haunted Carousel, Prospect Park
candidates.address: Children's Corner, Prospect Park (Flatbush Avenue entrance)
candidates.summary: The 1912 Prospect Park carousel gets a Halloween treatment Thursday October 29 through Sunday November 1, noon to 5pm, per the Prospect Park Alliance. Short rides, costumes encouraged, and it's a two-minute walk from the Flatbush Avenue entrance.
candidates.fit: A 1-year-old's first carousel ride in costume, twenty minutes from Fort Greene, and you're home by 2pm. The Halloween-weekend family option that doesn't involve a crowd of strangers in a parade.

candidates.title: Festival Neue Literatur 2026: Guests and Ghosts + Friedrich Ulfers Prize
candidates.summary: The main evening of Festival Neue Literatur, New York's German-language literature festival run jointly by Deutsches Haus at NYU, the German, Austrian and Swiss consulates and the Goethe-Institut. Authors Michael Lentz, Tanja Paar, Laura Vogt and Jonas Hassen Khemiri in conversation with translator Alta Price, plus the Friedrich Ulfers Prize. Tuesday October 27, 6:30 to 8pm at Irving Place; a companion session runs Monday October 26 at Deutsches Haus.
candidates.fit: The German-speaking cultural establishment in New York all in one room, in German and English, with free wine afterwards. Low-key, not a Time Out pick, and a soft entry point into the German community he keeps circling.

candidates.title: Samuel Weber: Giving and Taking — Hamann's Metakritik of Kant
candidates.summary: Public lecture by Samuel Weber at Deutsches Haus at NYU, the carriage-house building on Washington Mews, Friday October 16, 5:30 to 7pm. Deutsches Haus events are open to the public and free; the room holds well under 100.
candidates.fit: Pure deep-end German intellectual life in a 60-seat room — the opposite of a listicle. Worth it mainly as a way into the Deutsches Haus orbit, which also runs the children's program and the St. Martin's celebration he'll want in November.

candidates.title: Tammam Azzam: A Horizon Remains
candidates.summary: First New York solo show and first US institutional presentation of the Syrian-German artist Tammam Azzam, on view at the Goethe-Institut on Irving Place through November 15, 2026. Free admission. Listed as an ongoing exhibition on the Goethe-Institut New York calendar.
candidates.fit: A free, twenty-minute stop that pairs with any of the Goethe evening events above, or with a cocktail at Raines Law Room four blocks away. Low effort, actual substance.

candidates.title: 718 Sessions: Danny Krivit (+ That Matt in the Bad Room)
candidates.price_text: $5 for the first 100 before 7pm, $15-$25 advance on RA, $30 at the door
candidates.summary: Benny Soto's long-running 718 Sessions brings Danny Krivit back to Good Room for a Sunday evening into night, with That Matt in the Bad Room and lights by Ariel. Doors 6pm, 21+, $5-$30 depending on when you buy. Monday Oct 12 is a holiday, so the late end doesn't cost you a workday.
candidates.fit: A room of a few hundred people, a DJ who actually plays records all night, and a party that survives on word of mouth rather than marketing - the opposite of the listicle stuff he's sick of. Sunday-evening timing with a holiday Monday means he can do it without blowing up the week with the 1-year-old.

candidates.title: RA25 World Tour: New York (Nick León, Galcher Lustwerk, Stacey Hotwaxx Hale b2b Kilopatrah Jones)
candidates.summary: Resident Advisor's 25th-anniversary world tour makes its only New York stop at Good Room, with Miami's Nick León headlining alongside Galcher Lustwerk, adobeprincess, Baalti and Detroit's Stacey Hotwaxx Hale going b2b with Kilopatrah Jones across both rooms, plus one unannounced name. Tickets via RA.
candidates.fit: Ten dates worldwide, one New York night, in a 600-capacity Greenpoint club rather than a shed - exactly the 'you had to know about it' booking he wants, and the kind of lineup he can credibly put in the group chat on a Friday.

candidates.title: Goth Night at All Night Skate
candidates.summary: All Night Skate's spooky-season Goth Night with live performances from bluanxxiety, posterboy 2000 and meadow.le.elle, DJ sets from sssspikeee, Eros Hedonista and grrrrlafraid, plus tarot readings and flash tattoos. Doors 7pm, 21+, $5 suggested donation, nuns free.
candidates.fit: He already loves All Night Skate, it's a Thursday, it's five dollars, and it's the darkwave-costume-weirdo version of the bar programming he goes for. Tarot and stick-and-poke in the corner is the interactive part.

candidates.title: Armin van Buuren (extended set) at Brooklyn Storehouse
candidates.summary: Dreamland and Insomniac bring Armin van Buuren back to Brooklyn Storehouse for an extended set, with support from Hannah Laing and Ruben de Ronde, as part of the warehouse's closing season. Tickets via DICE and the venue's link.
candidates.fit: The big-warehouse-spectacle slot he budgets for a few times a year, in the same lane as the Kx5 night that is still his benchmark. If he wants one loud Friday with the guys this month, this is it.

candidates.title: ARRIVAL - The Hits of ABBA
candidates.summary: The long-running ABBA tribute show plays Kings Theatre in Flatbush on Thursday Oct 8, part of a two-week run of music and performance the theatre is promoting. Tickets through the Kings Theatre site; the venue has not posted a price publicly.
candidates.fit: He dressed up for an ABBA night in the West Village and loved it, and this is the full disco-boots version inside the most beautiful room in Brooklyn. Thursday is his night, and Flatbush is a short hop from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Meshuganah Mambo at Barbes
candidates.summary: Meshuganah Mambo play a tropical-klezmer dance set at Barbes on Friday Oct 9 at 8pm, with percussion, organ, sax, drums and bass. Barbes is a back room that holds well under a hundred people and runs on a suggested donation at the door.
candidates.fit: Klezmer in a tiny room is literally on his list, and this is the dancing version rather than the museum version. Easy early-evening date night that ends before midnight.

candidates.title: Hearts & Diamonds: Midnight Magic (live) with Three of Hearts and Pretty Girl
candidates.summary: Public Records' Sound Room hosts a live set from Brooklyn disco band Midnight Magic with the Three of Hearts DJs (Rok One, Andi, Danny White) and a Pretty Girl DJ set, on Thursday Oct 8. Tickets via DICE through the venue's link.
candidates.fit: Public Records is the best-sounding small room in his radius and a Thursday live disco band into DJs is a low-risk, high-quality version of his main night out. Fifteen minutes from Fort Greene.

candidates.title: Public Records x Gentle Time Farming harvest dinner
candidates.summary: Public Records' kitchen cooks alongside Gentle Time Farming, a trans- and queer-owned co-op growing East Asian vegetables for New York communities, for a one-night dinner marking the end of their growing season. Friday Oct 9; the venue has not posted a price in its announcement.
candidates.fit: One-night-only guest-kitchen collaboration is exactly the food bucket he asks for, and it's in a building he already trusts. Good wife dinner with a DJ upstairs afterward if the babysitter is flexible.

candidates.title: Mister Sunday (Eamon Harkin and Justin Carter)
candidates.price_text: RSVP on RA for $10 off the door before 4pm, $5 off before 5pm
candidates.summary: Nowadays' long-running outdoor Sunday party runs weekly between the poplar trees until Nov 1, with residents Eamon Harkin and Justin Carter playing 3pm to 9pm. RSVP on Resident Advisor knocks money off the door.
candidates.fit: Daytime dancing outdoors with the guys, done by dinner - the closest weekly thing to the BQE day party he still talks about, and one of the last outdoor Sundays of the year. Holiday Monday makes Oct 11 the right one to pick.

candidates.title: B3K Invites NY: Brutalismus 3000, SPFDJ, Dorian Electra, Eera, Nurse
candidates.summary: Berlin duo Brutalismus 3000 headline a special edition of the RUSH party at Knockdown Center on Friday Nov 6, with SPFDJ, Dorian Electra, Eera and Nurse. Presale opened Oct 6 at 10am, general on-sale 1pm the same day, via DICE.
candidates.fit: This is the loud Berlin end of his taste - German, fast, and nothing a listicle would send him to. Tickets went on sale this week, so it's a book-now item.

candidates.title: Circoloco Halloween New York (plus added Sunday day session)
candidates.time_text: Fri and Sat nights; Sunday Nov 1 runs 12pm to 12am
candidates.summary: Circoloco takes over Brooklyn Storehouse for Halloween weekend with Rampa, &ME, Seth Troxler, Mochakk, Carlita and more across Friday Oct 30 and Saturday Oct 31, and a newly added Sunday Nov 1 session running noon to midnight with Dixon, Bedouin, Chloe Caillet, Jimi Jules, Prospa and Rossi.
candidates.fit: Dixon and Jimi Jules on a Sunday afternoon, in costume, in a warehouse, is the Halloween version of the big melodic night he saves up for. The Sunday daytime pass is the dad-friendly way to do Circoloco.

candidates.title: Ahmed Spins at Knockdown Center
candidates.summary: Deep House Bible co-founder Ahmed Spins headlines the Knockdown Center Main Hall on Saturday Oct 24, playing the late shift from 11pm to 5am after his label takeover in The Ruins earlier this year. Tickets on RA and DICE.
candidates.fit: South African Afro-house is the bridge between his amapiano phase and his melodic house core, and this is the serious version of it rather than a bottle-service Afrobeats night. Late one, so it's a sometimes pick.

candidates.title: Massano and Konstantin at Knockdown Center
candidates.summary: Knockdown Center's October calendar lists Massano and Konstantin on Friday Oct 23. Tickets through the venue's DICE and RA links; the venue's post did not list set times or price.
candidates.fit: Massano is straight-down-the-middle melodic techno for someone whose top artist is deadmau5, and Konstantin brings the Giegling-school depth. Worth watching for the full lineup before booking.

candidates.title: Redirect with S'aint Panic
candidates.summary: The Redirect party returns to Good Room on Thursday Oct 22 with S'aint Panic in the big room, playing an open-format set spanning hard house, Baltimore club, vogue beats and melodic techno. Good Room's main room holds a few hundred people.
candidates.fit: A Thursday party run by a small Brooklyn collective, with a resident DJ nobody outside the scene has heard of - this is the word-of-mouth lane he keeps asking for, not a headliner show.

candidates.title: German Movie Nights: A LAND WITHIN, with director Michael Kofler
candidates.summary: The German Film Office screens A Land Within, a drama about separatist violence and family loyalty in German-speaking South Tyrol, at the Goethe-Institut on Wednesday Oct 14 at 7pm. Director Michael Kofler attends; registration is free via the link in their bio.
candidates.fit: German-language film with the director in the room, free, in a small institute space - the German-culture lane he wants fed, and an easy midweek thing that doesn't require a babysitter marathon.

candidates.title: HALLOWEENIX: Witch, PLEASE!
candidates.summary: Phoenix's Halloween costume dance party, hosted by Penny Livonia, Matzah Belle Soup and Giardia the Parasite as the Sanderson Sisters, with DJ Twink Death. Saturday Oct 31 from 10pm, no cover, costume contest with a $100 cash prize.
candidates.fit: He's already done a drag night at Phoenix with the guys and liked it; this is that plus costumes, on Halloween, with no cover and no table minimum anywhere in sight.

candidates.title: Phoenix Bar Annual Pumpkin Carving Contest
candidates.price_text: $10 for a pumpkin and carving kit, with a drink purchase
candidates.summary: Phoenix runs its annual pumpkin carving contest on Sunday Oct 18 from 5pm to 9pm. Ten dollars gets you a pumpkin and a carving kit, valid with a drink purchase.
candidates.fit: Cheap, hands-on, slightly stupid bar programming at a bar he already likes - he participates instead of watching, which is the whole point for him.

candidates.title: Halloween Night: comedians perform in character, with audience costume contest
candidates.summary: Hosted by Brittany Carney, a lineup including Jenny Zigrino, Don Will, Ike Ufomadu and others perform their stand-up entirely in costume and in character on Saturday Oct 31. There's an audience costume contest with prizes. Tickets at littlefieldnyc.com.
candidates.fit: Small-room stand-up with a gimmick he can participate in, and an early enough show that Halloween night isn't over at 7:30. Good one to drag two friends to in costume.

candidates.title: Let's Watch A Movie: THE BLAIR WITCH PROJECT
candidates.summary: Nostalgiarama's interactive screening series takes on The Blair Witch Project at Nitehawk Williamsburg on Monday Oct 26, with drag performances from Emigrate, Sterling Tull and Benedick the Bastard, live commentary, drinking games and prizes. Tickets via Nitehawk.
candidates.fit: The Rocky Horror-in-Flatbush format: a movie you shout at, with drag in front of it and a drink in your hand. Monday is a stretch, but he trains in Williamsburg anyway.

candidates.title: Brooklyn Horror Film Fest badge pickup party
candidates.summary: Brooklyn Horror Film Festival opens its badge pickup at KCBC on Monday Oct 12 from 5pm to 7pm, with horror bingo hosted by XG Horror, the first pour of the festival's 11th-anniversary beer, and free drink tickets for badge holders. Open to everyone, badge or not.
candidates.fit: Free, two hours, in a Bushwick brewery, and full of people who run the city's horror scene - the kind of low-key community thing he'd never find on a listings site. Easy holiday-Monday stop.

candidates.title: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong, three nights
candidates.summary: Pigeons Playing Ping Pong play three nights at Brooklyn Bowl, Nov 19 to 21, with Telula, Sqwerv and Slapdragon opening on successive nights. Tickets via the band's link and brooklynbowl.com.
candidates.fit: They're in his library already, the Thursday Nov 19 date lands on his night, and Brooklyn Bowl is a room where you can see the band and still get a drink without a line.

candidates.title: Threes Brewing Flea Market, Fall Edition
candidates.summary: Threes Brewing's Greenpoint taproom hosts its second flea market on Sunday Oct 18, noon to 6pm, curated by Fig Shop with local art, vintage clothing and accessories. Free to attend, RSVP via their link.
candidates.fit: Sunday daytime with a stroller, beer for him, something to actually look at - the brewery-yard hang he likes, with a reason to be there beyond drinking.

candidates.title: The Blaze (live)
candidates.summary: French duo The Blaze bring a special live set to the Knockdown Center Main Hall on Wednesday Oct 28. Artist presale ran Sept 30, public on-sale Oct 2; tickets via the venue's links.
candidates.fit: Cinematic French electronic played live is the Polo and Pan / Daft Punk touchstone end of his taste, and The Blaze's live show is a genuine spectacle. A Wednesday, so only if he's willing to spend one.

candidates.title: Festival Neue Literatur 2026: Guests and Ghosts
candidates.summary: The 16th edition of the German-language and US fiction festival runs Oct 26 to 29, with the New York events on Oct 26 and 27, featuring Michael Lentz, Tanja Paar, Laura Vogt, Jonas Hassen Khemiri and Nicole Krauss, plus the Friedrich Ulfers Prize to Peter Wortsman.
candidates.fit: The German-literary-scene night, in a small institute room rather than a theater. Worth it for him if one of the readings lands on a night he can get out; check which event is which before booking.

candidates.title: Bathhouse Atlantic Avenue: new heated backyard pool and outdoor sauna
candidates.price_text: included with a day pass or massage booking
candidates.summary: As of Oct 3, Bathhouse's Atlantic Avenue location has opened a year-round heated outdoor pool and outdoor sauna in its backyard, accessible with any day pass or massage booking. Lounge chairs are first come, first served.
candidates.fit: He's done the full Russian bathhouse day and wants more of it; this is the closest serious contrast-therapy setup to Fort Greene, and the outdoor pool in October is the good version of it. Go on a cold Saturday morning with one friend.
